| f-1a1a | defect | NIT | NIT (round 3, 09509b75) — the widened sweep parser now DERIVES age from entropy bits, with no plausibility bound. To make `fs3_migrations_&lt;32hex&gt;` and `fs3_storelock_&lt;32hex&gt;_&lt;worker&gt;` sweepable, `test_database_created_at` special-cases both prefixes and calls `unique_seed_created_at`, which is `Some((seed as u64) / 1_000_000_000)` — it takes the low 64 bits of the seed and divides by a billion, with no range check at all. For names this repo mints the decode is correct, because `unique_seed` puts nanos in the low 64 bits and XORs pid and a counter only above bit 64. But the sweep's age decision for these two shapes is now coupled to that bit layout, and nothing tests the coupling. If `unique_seed` is ever reordered, every such name silently gets a garbage age: uniformly distributed low-64 bits decode to roughly ten percent below the current epoch, i.e. immediately sweepable, and the rest to far-future dates that are never swept. The dangerous direction is the cheap one to close. Smallest fix: clamp the decode to a plausible window (reject anything before, say, 2020 or after now plus a day) so a garbage decode can never read as ancient, and add one test asserting that `unique_seed_created_at(format!("{:032x}", unique_seed()))` is within a few seconds of now, which pins the coupling the parser depends on. | crates/testkit/src/fresh_database.rs test_database_created_at and unique_seed_created_at at 09509b75 | [x] checked | — | — | — | [acceptance-criteria](../../plan.dd.md#acceptance-criteria) | Both functions read back in full at 09509b75. unique_seed_created_at performs a length and hex check and then returns (seed as u64)/1e9 with no lower or upper bound; unique_seed places nanos in the low 64 bits, XORing pid at bit 64 and a sequence counter at bit 96, so the decode is correct only while that layout holds. |
